verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν ὄχλον ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ καὶ ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἑστὼς παρὰ τὴν λίμνην Γεννησαρέτ
verses.transliteration: Egeneto de en tō ton ochlon epikeisthai autō kai akouein ton logon tou Theou kai autos ēn hestōs para tēn limnēn Gennēsaret
verses.literal: On one occasion . . . while . . . Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God
verses.literalPt: E ACONTECEU que, apertando-o a multidão, para ouvir a palavra de Deus, estava ele junto ao lago de Genesaré;

verses.original: καὶ εἶδεν πλοῖα δύο ἑστῶτα παρὰ τὴν λίμνην οἱ δὲ ἁλιεῖς ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀποβάντες ἔπλυνον τὰ δίκτυα
verses.transliteration: kai eiden ploia dyo hestōta para tēn limnēn hoi de halieis ap’ autōn apobantes eplynon ta diktya
verses.literal: He saw two boats at the edge of the lake The fishermen had left . . . them and were washing their nets
verses.literalPt: E viu estar dois barcos junto à praia do lago; e os pescadores, havendo descido deles, estavam lavando as redes.

verses.original: ἐμβὰς δὲ εἰς ἓν τῶν πλοίων ὃ ἦν Σίμωνος ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐπαναγαγεῖν ὀλίγον καθίσας δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐδίδασκεν τοὺς ὄχλους
verses.transliteration: embas de eis hen tōn ploiōn ho ēn Simōnos ērōtēsen auton apo tēs gēs epanagagein oligon kathisas de ek tou ploiou edidasken tous ochlous
verses.literal: Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore And sitting down He taught the people from the boat
verses.literalPt: E, entrando num dos barcos, que era o de Simão, pediu-lhe que o afastasse um pouco da terra; e, assentando-se, ensinava do barco a multidão.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα Ἐπανάγαγε εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ χαλάσατε τὰ δίκτυα ὑμῶν εἰς ἄγραν
verses.transliteration: Hōs de epausato lalōn eipen pros ton Simōna Epanagage eis to bathos kai chalasate ta diktya hymōn eis agran
verses.literal: When Jesus had finished speaking He said to Simon Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch
verses.literalPt: E, quando acabou de falar, disse a Simão: Faze-te ao mar alto, e lançai as vossas redes para pescar.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν Ἐπιστάτα δι’ ὅλης νυκτὸς κοπιάσαντες οὐδὲν ἐλάβομεν ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ῥήματί σου χαλάσω τὰ δίκτυα
verses.transliteration: Kai apokritheis Simōn eipen Epistata di’ holēs nyktos kopiasantes ouden elabomen epi de tō rhēmati sou chalasō ta diktya
verses.literal: Master Simon replied we have worked hard all night without catching anything But because You say so I will let down the nets
verses.literalPt: E, respondendo Simão, disse-lhe: Mestre, havendo trabalhado toda a noite, nada apanhamos; mas, sobre a tua palavra, lançarei a rede.

verses.original: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντες συνέκλεισαν πλῆθος ἰχθύων πολύ διερρήσσετο δὲ τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: kai touto poiēsantes synekleisan plēthos ichthyōn poly dierrēsseto de ta diktya autōn
verses.literal: When they had done so they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear
verses.literalPt: E, fazendo assim, colheram uma grande quantidade de peixes, e rompia-se-lhes a rede.

verses.original: καὶ κατένευσαν τοῖς μετόχοις ἐν τῷ ἑτέρῳ πλοίῳ τοῦ ἐλθόντας συλλαβέσθαι αὐτοῖς καὶ ἦλθον καὶ ἔπλησαν ἀμφότερα τὰ πλοῖα ὥστε βυθίζεσθαι αὐτά
verses.transliteration: kai kateneusan tois metochois en tō heterō ploiō tou elthontas syllabesthai autois kai ēlthon kai eplēsan amphotera ta ploia hōste bythizesthai auta
verses.literal: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink
verses.literalPt: E fizeram sinal aos companheiros que estavam no outro barco, para que os fossem ajudar. E foram, e encheram ambos os barcos, de maneira tal que quase iam a pique.

verses.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος προσέπεσεν τοῖς γόνασιν Ἰησοῦ λέγων Ἔξελθε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι Κύριε
verses.transliteration: Idōn de Simōn Petros prosepesen tois gonasin Iēsou legōn Exelthe ap’ emou hoti anēr hamartōlos eimi Kyrie
verses.literal: When Simon Peter saw this he fell at Jesus’ knees Go away from me Lord he said for I am a sinful man
verses.literalPt: E vendo isto Simão Pedro, prostrou-se aos pés de Jesus, dizendo: Senhor, ausenta-te de mim, que sou um homem pecador.

verses.original: θάμβος γὰρ περιέσχεν αὐτὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἄγρᾳ τῶν ἰχθύων ὧν συνέλαβον
verses.transliteration: thambos gar perieschen auton kai pantas tous syn autō epi tē agra tōn ichthyōn hōn synelabon
verses.literal: For he and his companions . . . . . . were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken
verses.literalPt: Pois que o espanto se apoderara dele, e de todos os que com ele estavam, por causa da pesca de peixe que haviam feito.

verses.original: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοὶ τῷ Σίμωνι Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μὴ φοβοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀνθρώπους ἔσῃ ζωγρῶν
verses.transliteration: homoiōs de kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn huious Zebedaiou hoi ēsan koinōnoi tō Simōni Kai eipen pros ton Simōna ho Iēsous Mē phobou apo tou nyn anthrōpous esē zōgrōn
verses.literal: and so were . . . - his partners James and John the sons of Zebedee Do not be afraid - Jesus said to Simon From now on you will catch men
verses.literalPt: E, de igual modo, também de Tiago e João, filhos de Zebedeu, que eram companheiros de Simão. E disse Jesus a Simão: Não temas; de agora em diante serás pescador de homens.

verses.original: καὶ καταγαγόντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἀφέντες πάντα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: kai katagagontes ta ploia epi tēn gēn aphentes panta ēkolouthēsan autō
verses.literal: And when they had brought their boats ashore they left everything and followed Him
verses.literalPt: E, levando os barcos para terra, deixaram tudo, e o seguiram.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν μιᾷ τῶν πόλεων καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ πλήρης λέπρας ἰδὼν δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐδεήθη αὐτοῦ λέγων Κύριε ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι
verses.transliteration: Kai egeneto en tō einai auton en mia tōn poleōn kai idou anēr plērēs lepras idōn de ton Iēsoun pesōn epi prosōpon edeēthē autou legōn Kyrie ean thelēs dynasai me katharisai
verses.literal: While . . . . . . Jesus was in one of the towns a man came along who was covered with leprosy When he saw Jesus he fell facedown and begged Him Lord if You are willing You can make me clean . . .
verses.literalPt: E aconteceu que, quando estava numa daquelas cidades, eis que um homem cheio de lepra, vendo a Jesus, prostrou-se sobre o rosto, e rogou-lhe, dizendo: Senhor, se quiseres, bem podes limpar-me.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ λέγων Θέλω καθαρίσθητι καὶ εὐθέως ἡ λέπρα ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai ekteinas tēn cheira hēpsato autou legōn Thelō katharisthēti kai eutheōs hē lepra apēlthen ap’ autou
verses.literal: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man I am willing He said Be clean And immediately the leprosy left . . . him
verses.literalPt: E ele, estendendo a mão, tocou-lhe, dizendo: Quero, sê limpo. E logo a lepra desapareceu dele.

verses.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς παρήγγειλεν αὐτῷ μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν Ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν δεῖξον σεαυτὸν τῷ ἱερεῖ καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου καθὼς προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: Kai autos parēngeilen autō mēdeni eipein Alla apelthōn deixon seauton tō hierei kai prosenenke peri tou katharismou sou kathōs prosetaxen Mōusēs eis martyrion autois
verses.literal: Do not tell anyone Jesus instructed him But go show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing as a testimony to them
verses.literalPt: E ordenou-lhe que a ninguém o dissesse. Mas vai, disse, mostra-te ao sacerdote, e oferece, pela tua purificação, o que Moisés determinou, para que lhes sirva de testemunho.

verses.original: Διήρχετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ συνήρχοντο ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀκούειν καὶ θεραπεύεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀσθενειῶν αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Diērcheto de mallon ho logos peri autou kai synērchonto ochloi polloi akouein kai therapeuesthai apo tōn astheneiōn autōn
verses.literal: But the news about Jesus spread all the more and great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses
verses.literalPt: A sua fama, porém, se propagava ainda mais, e ajuntava-se muita gente para o ouvir e para ser por ele curada das suas enfermidades.

verses.original: αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις καὶ προσευχόμενος
verses.transliteration: autos de ēn hypochōrōn en tais erēmois kai proseuchomenos
verses.literal: Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray
verses.literalPt: Ele, porém, retirava-se para os desertos, e ali orava.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ καὶ δύναμις Κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Kai egeneto en mia tōn hēmerōn kai autos ēn didaskōn kai ēsan kathēmenoi Pharisaioi kai nomodidaskaloi hoi ēsan elēlythotes ek pasēs kōmēs tēs Galilaias kai Ioudaias kai Ierousalēm kai dynamis Kyriou ēn eis to iasthai auton
verses.literal: One day Jesus was teaching and the Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there People had come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea and the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick
verses.literalPt: E aconteceu que, num daqueles dias, estava ensinando, e estavam ali assentados fariseus e doutores da lei, que tinham vindo de todas as aldeias da Galiléia, e da Judéia, e de Jerusalém. E a virtude do Senhor estava com ele para curar.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες φέροντες ἐπὶ κλίνης ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν καὶ θεῖναι αὐτὸν ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai idou andres pherontes epi klinēs anthrōpon hos ēn paralelymenos kai ezētoun auton eisenenkein kai theinai auton enōpion autou
verses.literal: Just then . . . some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat They tried to bring him inside . . . to set him before Jesus
verses.literalPt: E eis que uns homens transportaram numa cama um homem que estava paralítico, e procuravam fazê-lo entrar e pô-lo diante dele.

verses.original: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ποίας εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα διὰ τῶν κεράμων καθῆκαν αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ κλινιδίῳ εἰς τὸ μέσον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai mē heurontes poias eisenenkōsin auton dia ton ochlon anabantes epi to dōma dia tōn keramōn kathēkan auton syn tō klinidiō eis to meson emprosthen tou Iēsou
verses.literal: but they could not find a way - through the crowd So they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd right in front of Jesus
verses.literalPt: E, não achando por onde o pudessem levar, por causa da multidão, subiram ao telhado, e por entre as telhas o baixaram com a cama, até ao meio, diante de Jesus.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἄνθρωπε ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου
verses.transliteration: Kai idōn tēn pistin autōn eipen Anthrōpe apheōntai soi hai hamartiai sou
verses.literal: When Jesus saw their faith He said Friend your sins are forgiven . . .
verses.literalPt: E, vendo ele a fé deles, disse-lhe: Homem, os teus pecados te são perdoados.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤρξαντο διαλογίζεσθαι οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὃς λαλεῖ βλασφημίας τίς δύναται ἁμαρτίας ἀφεῖναι εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ Θεός
verses.transliteration: Kai ērxanto dialogizesthai hoi grammateis kai hoi Pharisaioi legontes Tis estin houtos hos lalei blasphēmias tis dynatai hamartias apheinai ei mē monos ho Theos
verses.literal: But the scribes and Pharisees began thinking to themselves . . . Who is this man who speaks blasphemy Who can forgive sins but . . . God alone
verses.literalPt: E os escribas e os fariseus começaram a arrazoar, dizendo: Quem é este que diz blasfêmias? Quem pode perdoar pecados, senão só Deus?

verses.original: Ἐπιγνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: Epignous de ho Iēsous tous dialogismous autōn apokritheis eipen pros autous Ti dialogizesthe en tais kardiais hymōn
verses.literal: Knowing what they were thinking Jesus replied . . . . . . . . . Why are you thinking these things in your hearts
verses.literalPt: Jesus, porém, conhecendo os seus pensamentos, respondeu, e disse-lhes: Que arrazoais em vossos corações?

verses.original: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον εἰπεῖν Ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου ἢ εἰπεῖν Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει
verses.transliteration: ti estin eukopōteron eipein Apheōntai soi hai hamartiai sou ē eipein Egeire kai peripatei
verses.literal: Which is easier to say Your sins are forgiven . . . or to say Get up and walk
verses.literalPt: Qual é mais fácil? dizer: Os teus pecados te são perdoados; ou dizer: Levanta-te, e anda?

verses.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας εἶπεν τῷ παραλελυμένῳ Σοὶ λέγω ἔγειρε καὶ ἄρας τὸ κλινίδιόν σου πορεύου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου
verses.transliteration: hina de eidēte hoti ho Huios tou anthrōpou exousian echei epi tēs gēs aphienai hamartias eipen tō paralelymenō Soi legō egeire kai aras to klinidion sou poreuou eis ton oikon sou
verses.literal: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins… He said to the paralytic I tell you get up pick up your mat and go home
verses.literalPt: Ora, para que saibais que o Filho do homem tem sobre a terra poder de perdoar pecados (disse ao paralítico), a ti te digo: Levanta-te, toma a tua cama, e vai para tua casa.

verses.original: Καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀναστὰς ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ἄρας ἐφ’ ὃ κατέκειτο ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ δοξάζων τὸν Θεόν
verses.transliteration: Kai parachrēma anastas enōpion autōn aras eph’ ho katekeito apēlthen eis ton oikon autou doxazōn ton Theon
verses.literal: And immediately the man stood up before them took what he had been lying on and went home glorifying God
verses.literalPt: E, levantando-se logo diante deles, e tomando a cama em que estava deitado, foi para sua casa, glorificando a Deus.

verses.original: καὶ ἔκστασις ἔλαβεν ἅπαντας καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν Θεόν καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν φόβου λέγοντες ὅτι Εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον
verses.transliteration: kai ekstasis elaben hapantas kai edoxazon ton Theon kai eplēsthēsan phobou legontes hoti Eidomen paradoxa sēmeron
verses.literal: Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God They were filled with awe and said We have seen remarkable things today
verses.literalPt: E todos ficaram maravilhados, e glorificaram a Deus; e ficaram cheios de temor, dizendo: Hoje vimos prodígios.

verses.original: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἐθεάσατο τελώνην ὀνόματι Λευὶν καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀκολούθει μοι
verses.transliteration: Kai meta tauta exēlthen kai etheasato telōnēn onomati Leuin kathēmenon epi to telōnion kai eipen autō Akolouthei moi
verses.literal: After this Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth Follow Me He told him
verses.literalPt: E, depois disto, saiu, e viu um publicano, chamado Levi, assentado na recebedoria, e disse-lhe: Segue-me.

verses.original: καὶ καταλιπὼν πάντα ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: kai katalipōn panta anastas ēkolouthei autō
verses.literal: and Levi got up left everything and followed Him
verses.literalPt: E ele, deixando tudo, levantou-se e o seguiu.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐποίησεν δοχὴν μεγάλην Λευὶς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἦν ὄχλος πολὺς τελωνῶν καὶ ἄλλων οἳ ἦσαν μετ’ αὐτῶν κατακείμενοι
verses.transliteration: Kai epoiēsen dochēn megalēn Leuis autō en tē oikia autou kai ēn ochlos polys telōnōn kai allōn hoi ēsan met’ autōn katakeimenoi
verses.literal: Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house A large crowd of tax collectors was there along with others who were eating with them
verses.literalPt: E fez-lhe Levi um grande banquete em sua casa; e havia ali uma multidão de publicanos e outros que estavam com eles à mesa.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγόγγυζον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίετε καὶ πίνετε
verses.transliteration: kai egongyzon hoi Pharisaioi kai hoi grammateis autōn pros tous mathētas autou legontes Dia ti meta tōn telōnōn kai hamartōlōn esthiete kai pinete
verses.literal: But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to Jesus’ disciples Why . . . do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners
verses.literalPt: E os escribas deles, e os fariseus, murmuravam contra os seus discípulos, dizendo: Por que comeis e bebeis com publicanos e pecadores?

verses.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ὑγιαίνοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες
verses.transliteration: Kai apokritheis ho Iēsous eipen pros autous Ou chreian echousin hoi hygiainontes iatrou alla hoi kakōs echontes
verses.literal: Jesus answered . . . . . . . . . It is not the healthy who need a doctor but the sick . . .
verses.literalPt: E Jesus, respondendo, disse-lhes: Não necessitam de médico os que estão sãos, mas, sim, os que estão enfermos;

verses.original: οὐκ ἐλήλυθα καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν
verses.transliteration: ouk elēlytha kalesai dikaious alla hamartōlous eis metanoian
verses.literal: I have not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance
verses.literalPt: Eu não vim chamar os justos, mas, sim, os pecadores, ao arrependimento.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν Οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου νηστεύουσιν πυκνὰ καὶ δεήσεις ποιοῦνται ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ τῶν Φαρισαίων οἱ δὲ σοὶ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ πίνουσιν
verses.transliteration: Hoi de eipan pros auton Hoi mathētai Iōannou nēsteuousin pykna kai deēseis poiountai homoiōs kai hoi tōn Pharisaiōn hoi de soi esthiousin kai pinousin
verses.literal: Then they said to Him John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray but Yours keep on eating and drinking
verses.literalPt: Disseram-lhe, então, eles: Por que jejuam os discípulos de João muitas vezes, e fazem orações, como também os dos fariseus, mas os teus comem e bebem?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Μὴ δύνασθε τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ποιῆσαι νηστεῦσαι
verses.transliteration: Ho de Iēsous eipen pros autous Mē dynasthe tous huious tou nymphōnos en hō ho nymphios met’ autōn estin poiēsai nēsteusai
verses.literal: Jesus replied . . . . . . Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them
verses.literalPt: E ele lhes disse: Podeis vós fazer jejuar os filhos das bodas, enquanto o esposo está com eles?

verses.original: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι καὶ ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις
verses.transliteration: eleusontai de hēmerai kai hotan aparthē ap’ autōn ho nymphios tote nēsteusousin en ekeinais tais hēmerais
verses.literal: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them then . . . . . . . . . . . . they will fast
verses.literalPt: Dias virão, porém, em que o esposo lhes será tirado, e então, naqueles dias, jejuarão.

verses.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ἀπὸ ἱματίου καινοῦ σχίσας ἐπιβάλλει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν εἰ δὲ μή¦γε καὶ τὸ καινὸν σχίσει καὶ τῷ παλαιῷ οὐ συμφωνήσει τὸ ἐπίβλημα τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ καινοῦ
verses.transliteration: Elegen de kai parabolēn pros autous hoti Oudeis epiblēma apo himatiou kainou schisas epiballei epi himation palaion ei de mē¦ge kai to kainon schisei kai tō palaiō ou symphōnēsei to epiblēma to apo tou kainou
verses.literal: He also told . . . . . . them a parable No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one If he does . . . . . . he will tear the new garment as well and the patch - from the new will not match the old
verses.literalPt: E disse-lhes também uma parábola: Ninguém tira um pedaço de uma roupa nova para a coser em roupa velha, pois romperá a nova e o remendo não condiz com a velha.

verses.original: Καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς εἰ δὲ μή¦γε ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος ὁ νέος τοὺς ἀσκούς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκχυθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπολοῦνται
verses.transliteration: Kai oudeis ballei oinon neon eis askous palaious ei de mē¦ge rhēxei ho oinos ho neos tous askous kai autos ekchythēsetai kai hoi askoi apolountai
verses.literal: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins If he does the new wine will burst the skins the wine will spill and the wineskins will be ruined
verses.literalPt: E ninguém deita vinho novo em odres velhos; de outra sorte o vinho novo romperá os odres, e entornar-se-á o vinho, e os odres se estragarão;

verses.original: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινοὺς βλητέον
verses.transliteration: alla oinon neon eis askous kainous blēteon
verses.literal: Instead new wine is poured into new wineskins
verses.literalPt: Mas o vinho novo deve deitar-se em odres novos, e ambos juntamente se conservarão.

verses.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς πιὼν παλαιὸν θέλει νέον λέγει γάρ Ὁ παλαιὸς χρηστός ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: kai oudeis piōn palaion thelei neon legei gar Ho palaios chrēstos estin
verses.literal: And no one after drinking old wine wants new for he says The old is better
verses.literalPt: E ninguém tendo bebido o velho quer logo o novo, porque diz: Melhor é o velho.
